defining_records.title: Whose Image and Superscription? Toward a Semantic Economics of the Mint (EA-SEI-MINT-01)

captures.description: SEMANTIC ECONOMICS OF THE MINT: the AI Overview gives Whose Image and Superscription? (#610) at grain — currency design as 'an economic and political compression layer', four phases from the Lydian stamp to 'The Return of the Sovereign' (a living president's signature, 'noted in the paper as occurring on March 26, 2026'), compressed portraiture, the restoration operator σ_SH, CC BY-SA as an unbranded centre — and keeps the MINT acronym apart; Rex Fraction is not named.

refers to a proposed interdisciplinary subdiscipline that analyzes the physical and design elements of currency—such as faces, seals, signatures, and inscriptions—as an economic and political compression layer rather than mere decoration
outlines this framework by combining monetary economics, numismatics, semiotics, political theory, and sociology

The concept of the semantic economics of the mint refers to a proposed interdisciplinary subdiscipline that analyzes the physical and design elements of currency—such as faces, seals, signatures, and inscriptions—as an economic and political compression layer rather than mere decoration.
